newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya deploys thousands of troops to break up protest.
newsitem.headline: Kenya deploys thousands of troops to break up protest.

text.p: Kenya deployed thousands of heavily armed troops in the centre of the capital Nairobi on Saturday after security forces broke up a rally by opposition and church leaders.
The bustling city centre was brought to a complete standstill as truckloads of police and troops were brought in to counter the show of opposition against the government of President Daniel arap Moi.
In other parts of the capital, business and traffic was disrupted after opposition followers stoned cars and engaged police units in running battles.
In the affluent suburb of Parklands, a Reuters correspondent saw cars being stoned and a white couple had their windscreen smashed by opposition youthhwingers but the family escaped unhurt.

Security forces armed with automatic rifles and in full riot gear fanned out across the city centre and strategic buildings such as parliament and the state-owned radio and television stations were ringed by troops.
Motorists trying to get into the city centre were turned back by police as reinforcements moved into the townships of Nairobi.
"You are safer staying at home than driving around Nairobi today," a police officer yelled at motorists on the main highway leading to the city.
A senior police officer told Reuters police and paramilitary units were under strict orders to stamp out pockets of lawlessness in the city. "We are acting on high-level orders," the officer said.
Police and paramilitary units earlier fired teargas grenades and wielded billyclubs to drive around 2,000 protesters out of central Uhuru Park and then fought battles with protesters.
Kenya's government declared the rally illegal on Friday, warning the public not to attend.
An aide to leading opposition politician, Kenneth Matiba, said his boss was meeting other opposition figures at a hideout in the city to plan their next move.
The government had warned the public not to attend the rally and said anyone attending would "face the full force of the law".
Matiba, a leading opposition leader and proponent of constitutional change, vowed to make Nairobi hell for Moi and his government.

"We will make the city hell for Moi and his cronies. I will not sleep tonight because I have to be with the people and this means Moi cannot sleep either because his security will have to keep on briefing him," Matiba told Reuters through his spokesman.
Matiba is the chairman of the opposition FORD-Asili party and is one the East African nation's leading businessmen.

The latest confrontation between protesters and security forces came after the National Convention Assembly (NCA), an umbrella for Protestant and Catholic church leaders and opposition parties, called the rally to press for a minimum package of constitutional reform before elections later this year.
